podcast.body: Following Creation Records' acquisition by Sony and an injection of funds, the label signed the then-unknown Oasis, who subsequently became leaders of the Britpop genre. Their second album, "(What's the Story) Morning Glory?", went on to become the best-selling British album of the decade, a significant commercial success for the revitalized label. "eso segundo álbum, Watch the Story, Modern Glory, se convirtió en el disco británico más vendido de la década."

podcast.body: Oasis's second album, from which the single "Roll With It" was released on August 15, 1995. This album, despite its quintessentially British hooks and cover shot locations (Burwick Street, Noel Avenue, Oxford Street), translated globally, selling over 10 million copies and making Oasis "the biggest band on the planet." "That second album wants the story morning glory."

podcast.body: Released in 1995, this album was a massive commercial success for Oasis, selling millions of copies globally, including in the challenging US market, establishing them as one of the biggest bands in the world by 1996. Its immense popularity paved the way for planned projects like the ill-fated MTV Unplugged album. "The What's The Story Morning glory album was selling by the Millions, even in the US, which is a very tough market for a British rock band to crack in those days."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released in August 1995, shortly after Blur's "Parklife," this album cemented Oasis's position as a dominant force in the Britpop movement. Oasis, being quite young, entered the scene with an unstoppable and fresh energy that contrasted with the more seasoned Blur.

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.body: Released in October 1995, this second album, though recorded very quickly due to Noel Gallagher's prolific songwriting, had its release delayed for approximately six months. The delay was a strategic decision by the record label to allow "Definitely Maybe" to continue its strong sales and chart performance without competition. Following a successful strategy of progressive single releases from April 1995, the album generated explosive demand and is widely regarded as the definitive Britpop album, significantly impacting modern pop and outperforming Blur in the "Great Britpop Battle." "Wossios, Tori Morninglor, es el disco de gripo con mayúsculas."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.body: Released on October 2, 1995, *What's the Story (Morning Glory)?* became an immediate sensation, selling one copy every two minutes on release day and 350,000 copies within its first week, making it the fastest-selling British album ever at that time. It sustained sales of 200,000 copies a week and propelled Oasis to become "the biggest band on Planet Earth." "It came out on schedule on October 2, 1995. And on that day, it sold at a rate of 1 every 2 minutes. Within a week, it sold 350,000 copies, making it the fastest selling British album ever to that point."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released on October 30, 1995, this album featured "Some Might Say" as its first single. "Wonderwall" was released as the fourth single, "Don't Look Back in Anger" as the fifth, and "Champagne Supernova" closed the album and was its sixth and final single. "leading up to the release of the Morning Glory album on October 30th."

podcast.body: The anniversary of this 1995 album in 2025 coincides with plans for a band reunion, suggesting a strategic timing for the Gallagher brothers' agreement to reunite. "what's the story morning glory from 1995?"

podcast.body: The initial release of this album included the song "Step Out." However, all subsequent editions of the album were issued without "Step Out," making the original version quite valuable. This removal was due to similarities with Stevie Wonder's "Uptight Everything's All Right," resulting in a court case where Wonder, Sylvia Moe, and Henry Cosby received writing credits and proceeds. "When they watched the story Morning Glory album first came out, it included a song called Step Out. However, all subsequent editions of Morning Glory were issued without that song making the original version quite valuable."

podcast.body: This album included the single "Roll With It", which was released in August 1995. While the single was considered relatively weaker than Blur's "Country House," the album itself was described as much more powerful, which helped prolong the "Great Battle of Britpop" for over a year. "como al final el disco, Oasis era mucho más potente, hubo ahí una pelea entre singles y discos que consiguieron alargarla durante más de un año."

podcast.body: This album originally included the song "Step Out." However, due to its strong resemblance to Stevie Wonder's 1966 hit "Uptight (Everything's All Right)," Wonder successfully claimed infringement, and "all subsequent editions of the album had that song removed." Post-Morning Glory versions credit "Noel Gallagher and three other people," reducing Noel's royalties to 25%. "This was also taken by Stevie Wonder over a song called Step Out from What's the Story Morning Glory album which sounded way too much life as 1966 hit Uptight Everything's All Right."

podcast.body: This album was a huge success for Oasis, which meant there was no one around to challenge the band's drug-fueled creative decisions for their subsequent record. "Because Oasis had just come off the huge success of what's the story. Morning glory, there was nobody around to tell them to stop and sober up and do things properly."

podcast.body: This album, released on October 2, 1995, became a massive global hit, selling close to 25 million copies worldwide. It significantly outsold Blur's "The Great Escape," despite Blur winning the single chart battle. "Once the story and morning glory became a massive global hit, selling close to 25,000,000 copies."
